category: WLAN, Bluetooth & Satellite Communications Toolboxes > Waveforms, Channels, Receivers & Scenarios
description: IEEE 802.11 (a/g/n/ac/ax/be) packet configuration, waveform generation, channel models and receiver functions from WLAN Toolbox; Bluetooth BR/EDR and LE waveform generation, ideal receivers and network nodes from Bluetooth Toolbox; and satellite scenario simulation, link analysis, propagation losses, GNSS codes and DVB-S2 waveforms from Satellite Communications Toolbox.

tools.name: wlanWaveformGenerator
tools.description: Generates a time-domain IEEE 802.11 waveform (one or more packets with idle time) from payload bits and a PHY configuration object for any supported format: non-HT (a/g), HT (n), VHT (ac), HE (ax), EHT (be), UHR, DMG, S1G and WUR. Options control packet count, idle time, scrambler seed, windowing and oversampling. Without arguments it opens the WLAN Waveform Generator app.
tools.usage:
waveform = wlanWaveformGenerator(bits, cfg)
waveform = wlanWaveformGenerator(bits, cfg, Name=Value)
wlanWaveformGenerator

parameters.name: bits
parameters.description: PSDU bits (vector), or cell array per user for multi-user formats; looped over packets.

parameters.name: cfg
parameters.description: wlanNonHTConfig, wlanHTConfig, wlanVHTConfig, wlanHESUConfig, wlanHEMUConfig, wlanHETBConfig, wlanEHTMUConfig, wlanDMGConfig, wlanS1GConfig, wlanWURConfig ...

tools.notes: Field boundaries within the packet are returned by wlanFieldIndices(cfg). Pass the waveform through wlanTGaxChannel/wlanTGnChannel, then use the format-specific recovery functions.

tools.name: wlanNonHTConfig
tools.description: Configuration object for a non-HT (802.11a/g/j/p) packet: OFDM or DSSS modulation, channel bandwidth (5/10/20 MHz), MCS 0-7 or DSSS data rate, PSDU length and transmit antennas. Non-HT PPDUs also carry control frames (ACK/RTS/CTS) for every later format.
tools.usage:
cfg = wlanNonHTConfig
cfg = wlanNonHTConfig(Name=Value)
tools.notes: Other config objects: wlanHTConfig (802.11n), wlanVHTConfig (ac), wlanHESUConfig/wlanHEMUConfig/wlanHETBConfig (ax), wlanEHTMUConfig (be), wlanS1GConfig (ah), wlanDMGConfig (ad).

tools.name: wlanHTConfig
tools.description: Configuration object for an 802.11n HT-mixed packet: 20/40 MHz bandwidth, MCS 0-31 (up to 4 spatial streams), space-time block coding, guard interval, aggregation flag, PSDU length and channel coding (BCC or LDPC). Used with wlanWaveformGenerator and the HT recovery functions (wlanHTDataRecover, wlanHTLTFChannelEstimate).
tools.usage:
cfg = wlanHTConfig
cfg = wlanHTConfig(Name=Value)

parameters.name: NumTransmitAntennas / NumSpaceTimeStreams
parameters.description: Antenna and STS counts (STBC when STS > streams).

tools.example:
cfg = wlanHTConfig(ChannelBandwidth='CBW40', MCS=13, NumTransmitAntennas=2, NumSpaceTimeStreams=2, PSDULength=2048);
tx = wlanWaveformGenerator(randi([0 1], 8*cfg.PSDULength, 1), cfg);
tools.notes: MCS 32 and unequal-modulation MCS are not supported. For 802.11ac use wlanVHTConfig with up to 8 streams and 160 MHz.

tools.name: wlanVHTConfig
tools.description: Configuration object for an 802.11ac VHT packet: 20 to 160 MHz bandwidth, MCS 0-9, up to 8 space-time streams, single- or multi-user (MU-MIMO with per-user MCS and stream counts), STBC, LDPC/BCC, beamforming via SpatialMapping and precoding matrix, and APEP/PSDU lengths.
tools.usage:
cfg = wlanVHTConfig
cfg = wlanVHTConfig(Name=Value)

parameters.name: APEPLength
parameters.description: A-MPDU pre-EOF padding length in bytes.

tools.example:
cfg = wlanVHTConfig(ChannelBandwidth='CBW80', MCS=9, NumTransmitAntennas=4, NumSpaceTimeStreams=4, APEPLength=4000);
tx = wlanWaveformGenerator(randi([0 1], 8*cfg.PSDULength, 1), cfg);
tools.notes: PSDULength is derived from APEPLength; read cfg.PSDULength before generating bits. VHT recovery: wlanVHTDataRecover, wlanVHTLTFChannelEstimate, wlanVHTSIGARecover.

tools.name: wlanHESUConfig
tools.description: Configuration object for an 802.11ax HE single-user (or extended-range) packet: bandwidth up to 160 MHz, MCS 0-11, guard interval and HE-LTF type, DCM, coding, spatial streams, midamble periodicity and APEP length. It is the starting point for HE link simulations together with wlanHEMUConfig (OFDMA/MU-MIMO) and wlanHETBConfig (trigger-based uplink).
tools.usage:
cfg = wlanHESUConfig
cfg = wlanHESUConfig(Name=Value)
tools.notes: HE recovery functions: wlanHEDataBitRecover, wlanHELTFChannelEstimate, wlanHESIGARecover, wlanHEDemodulate, wlanHEDataRecover (deprecated in favour of the bit-recover flow).

tools.name: wlanEHTMUConfig
tools.description: Configuration object for an 802.11be (Wi-Fi 7) EHT multi-user packet: bandwidth up to 320 MHz, OFDMA resource-unit allocation (including multiple RUs per user and puncturing), MCS 0-13 (4096-QAM), up to 8 spatial streams per user, EHT-LTF and guard interval settings. Single-user EHT packets are configured through the same object with one user.
tools.usage:
cfg = wlanEHTMUConfig(cbw)
cfg = wlanEHTMUConfig(cbw, Name=Value)
cfg = wlanEHTMUConfig(AllocationIndex)

parameters.name: AllocationIndex
parameters.description: Resource-unit allocation index per 20 MHz subchannel (table from the standard).

tools.notes: Introduced in R2022a and extended through later releases (multi-RU, 320 MHz, EHT TB via wlanEHTTBConfig). Use ruInfo(cfg) to inspect the RU layout.

tools.name: wlanFieldIndices
tools.description: Returns the start and end sample indices of each field of a packet (L-STF, L-LTF, L-SIG, format-specific SIG/STF/LTF fields and the data field) for a configuration object, so a receiver can slice a synchronized waveform into its preamble and payload parts.
tools.usage:
ind = wlanFieldIndices(cfg)
ind = wlanFieldIndices(cfg, field)
ind = wlanFieldIndices(cfg, 'OversamplingFactor', osf)

parameters.name: ind
parameters.description: Struct of [start end] uint32 pairs (samples at the nominal rate).

tools.notes: Indices assume the packet starts at sample 1; add the packet offset from wlanPacketDetect.

tools.name: wlanTGaxChannel
tools.description: System object implementing the 802.11ax TGax indoor MIMO channel model (delay profiles Model-A to Model-F, Doppler from environmental motion, large-scale path loss/shadowing, antenna spacing and polarization), used to fade HE/EHT waveforms in link simulations. Related objects: wlanTGnChannel (802.11n), wlanTGacChannel (802.11ac), wlanTGahChannel, wlanTGayChannel.
tools.usage:
chan = wlanTGaxChannel
chan = wlanTGaxChannel(Name=Value)
y = chan(x)
[y, pathGains] = chan(x)
tools.example:
chan = wlanTGaxChannel(SampleRate=wlanSampleRate(cfg), ChannelBandwidth='CBW80', DelayProfile='Model-D', NumTransmitAntennas=2, NumReceiveAntennas=2, LargeScaleFadingEffect='Pathloss and shadowing', TransmitReceiveDistance=15);
rx = chan([tx; zeros(50, 2)]);   % pad for channel delay
tools.notes: Call reset(chan) between packets for independent realizations; ChannelFiltering=false returns path gains only.

tools.name: wlanPacketDetect
tools.description: Detects the start of an 802.11 OFDM packet in a received waveform by autocorrelating the L-STF periodic structure, returning the sample offset of the packet start (or empty if none is found) and the autocorrelation metric. It is the first receiver stage before coarse CFO estimation and fine timing.
tools.usage:
startOffset = wlanPacketDetect(rx, cbw)
startOffset = wlanPacketDetect(rx, cbw, offset)
startOffset = wlanPacketDetect(rx, cbw, offset, threshold)
[startOffset, M] = wlanPacketDetect(___)
tools.notes: Typical chain: wlanPacketDetect -> wlanCoarseCFOEstimate -> wlanSymbolTimingEstimate -> wlanFineCFOEstimate -> wlanLLTFChannelEstimate -> wlanFormatDetect -> format-specific decode.

tools.name: wlanCoarseCFOEstimate
tools.description: Estimates the carrier frequency offset from the L-STF of a detected packet using the repetition of its short training symbols, returning the offset in Hz to be removed before timing synchronization. wlanFineCFOEstimate refines the estimate using the L-LTF.
tools.usage:
fOffset = wlanCoarseCFOEstimate(rxSig, cbw)
fOffset = wlanCoarseCFOEstimate(rxSig, cbw, corrOffset)

parameters.name: corrOffset
parameters.description: Correlation offset in symbols (0 to 1, default 0.75).

tools.notes: Coarse estimation range is +/- fs/(2*16*20 MHz basis) i.e. about +/-625 kHz at 20 MHz; fine estimation refines within +/-156 kHz.

tools.name: wlanLLTFChannelEstimate
tools.description: Estimates the channel from the demodulated L-LTF symbols (wlanLLTFDemodulate output), optionally smoothing across subcarriers, giving the estimate needed to decode L-SIG and the format-specific SIG fields (HT-SIG, VHT-SIG-A, HE-SIG-A) before the format-specific LTF estimates are available.
tools.usage:
est = wlanLLTFChannelEstimate(demodSig, cbw)
est = wlanLLTFChannelEstimate(demodSig, cfg)
est = wlanLLTFChannelEstimate(___, span)

parameters.name: demodSig
parameters.description: Output of wlanLLTFDemodulate (subcarriers x symbols x antennas).

parameters.name: span
parameters.description: Frequency smoothing filter span in subcarriers (odd integer).

tools.notes: Data-field decoding uses the format-specific estimates: wlanHTLTFChannelEstimate, wlanVHTLTFChannelEstimate, wlanHELTFChannelEstimate.

tools.name: wlanFormatDetect
tools.description: Detects the PHY format (Non-HT, HT-MF, HT-GF, VHT, HE-SU, HE-MU, HE-EXT-SU, HE-TB, EHT ...) of a received packet from the three OFDM symbols following the L-LTF, using the L-LTF channel estimate and noise variance, so the receiver can select the correct decoding path.
tools.usage:
format = wlanFormatDetect(rxSig, chanEst, noiseVarEst, cbw)
format = wlanFormatDetect(rxSig, chanEst, noiseVarEst, cbw, Name=Value)

parameters.name: rxSig
parameters.description: Samples from the start of L-SIG spanning at least 3 symbols.

parameters.name: chanEst, noiseVarEst
parameters.description: From wlanLLTFChannelEstimate and a noise estimate.

tools.notes: For HE and EHT the receiver then recovers HE-SIG-A/U-SIG fields to fill wlanHERecoveryConfig / wlanEHTRecoveryConfig before data decoding.

tools.name: wlanSampleRate
tools.description: Returns the nominal baseband sample rate of a WLAN configuration (20e6 for 20 MHz OFDM, 80e6 for 80 MHz, 1.76e9 for DMG, etc.), optionally scaled by an oversampling factor. Use it to set channel and impairment objects and for time/frequency conversions.
tools.usage:
fs = wlanSampleRate(cfg)
fs = wlanSampleRate(cbw)
fs = wlanSampleRate(___, 'OversamplingFactor', osf)

parameters.name: cfg / cbw
parameters.description: Configuration object or bandwidth string such as 'CBW40'.

tools.example:
fs = wlanSampleRate('CBW80')     % 8.0000e+07
chan = wlanTGacChannel(SampleRate=fs, ChannelBandwidth='CBW80');
tools.notes: Introduced in R2017b (replacing helperSampleRate).

tools.name: wlanMACFrame
tools.description: Generates an 802.11 MAC frame (data, management or control, including QoS data, beacon, ACK, RTS/CTS and A-MPDU/A-MSDU aggregation) from a wlanMACFrameConfig object and optional MSDU payload, returning the frame as bits or octets plus its length; used to build realistic PSDUs for wlanWaveformGenerator. wlanMPDUDecode parses received frames.
tools.usage:
[frame, frameLength] = wlanMACFrame(cfgMAC)
[frame, frameLength] = wlanMACFrame(payload, cfgMAC)
[frame, frameLength] = wlanMACFrame(payload, cfgMAC, cfgPHY)
[frame, frameLength] = wlanMACFrame(___, 'OutputFormat', 'bits')

parameters.name: payload
parameters.description: MSDU as octets (hex char/decimal) or cell array for aggregation.

parameters.name: cfgPHY
parameters.description: PHY config needed for A-MPDU padding rules.

tools.notes: wlanMACManagementConfig builds beacon/probe bodies; wlanMSDUAggregate/wlanAMPDUDeaggregate handle aggregation; wlanMPDUDecode returns FCS status.

tools.name: bluetoothWaveformGenerator
tools.description: Generates Bluetooth basic rate / enhanced data rate (BR/EDR) baseband waveforms for a packet type (DM/DH data, HV/EV SCO, POLL/NULL, etc.) and transmission mode (BR GFSK, EDR2M pi/4-DQPSK, EDR3M 8DPSK) from a bluetoothWaveformConfig, including access code, header, whitening and oversampling. bluetoothIdealReceiver decodes the result.
tools.usage: waveform = bluetoothWaveformGenerator(bits, cfg)

parameters.name: bits
parameters.description: Payload bits; length a multiple of the payload length (getPayloadLength(cfg)*8).

parameters.name: cfg
parameters.description: bluetoothWaveformConfig with Mode, PacketType, PayloadLength, SamplesPerSymbol, WhitenStatus, DeviceAddress, LogicalTransportAddress ...

tools.notes: Requires Bluetooth Toolbox (R2020b+ as a separate product; earlier in Communications Toolbox Library for Bluetooth). Bluetooth LE waveforms use bleWaveformGenerator instead.

tools.name: bluetoothWaveformConfig
tools.description: Configuration object describing a Bluetooth BR/EDR packet for waveform generation and ideal reception: mode (BR, EDR2M, EDR3M), packet type, payload length, device address, logical transport address, header fields (flow, ARQN, SEQN), whitening initialization, modulation index and samples per symbol.
tools.usage:
cfg = bluetoothWaveformConfig
cfg = bluetoothWaveformConfig(Name=Value)
len = getPayloadLength(cfg)
dur = bluetoothPacketDuration(cfg.Mode, cfg.PacketType, len)

parameters.name: DeviceAddress
parameters.description: 48-bit Bluetooth device address as hex string.

tools.notes: getPayloadLength returns the effective payload for the packet type; bluetoothPacketDuration gives on-air time in microseconds.

tools.name: bleWaveformGenerator
tools.description: Generates Bluetooth Low Energy PHY waveforms (LE1M, LE2M, LE500K, LE125K coded PHYs) from PDU bits with the given samples per symbol, channel index (for whitening), access address and optional direction-finding (AoA/AoD) constant tone extension configuration. bleIdealReceiver demodulates and decodes the waveform.
tools.usage:
waveform = bleWaveformGenerator(bits, phyMode, sps, chanIdx, accessAddr)
waveform = bleWaveformGenerator(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: bits
parameters.description: PDU bits (advertising or data channel PDU, e.g. from bleLLAdvertisingChannelPDU / bleLLDataChannelPDU).

tools.notes: Sample rate is sps*1e6 for LE1M/coded and sps*2e6 for LE2M. Full protocol-stack simulations use bluetoothLENode with wirelessNetworkSimulator.

tools.name: bleIdealReceiver
tools.description: Ideal Bluetooth LE receiver that performs timing synchronization, GMSK demodulation, dewhitening and (for coded PHYs) FEC decoding on a received LE waveform, returning the recovered PDU bits and detected access address. Used for BER/PER simulations with bleWaveformGenerator and channel/impairment models.
tools.usage:
bits = bleIdealReceiver(waveform, phyMode, sps, chanIdx)
[bits, accessAddr] = bleIdealReceiver(waveform, phyMode, sps, chanIdx)
[bits, accessAddr, iqSamples] = bleIdealReceiver(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: 'AccessAddress'
parameters.description: Expected access address for correlation-based sync.

parameters.name: 'DFPacketType' / 'DFConfig'
parameters.description: Direction-finding settings to extract CTE IQ samples.

tools.example:
[rxBits, rxAccess] = bleIdealReceiver(rx, 'LE2M', 8, 17);
numErr = biterr(pdu, rxBits(1:numel(pdu)));
tools.notes: For a practical receiver with CFO/timing recovery see the 'Bluetooth LE Receiver' examples; the BR/EDR counterpart is bluetoothIdealReceiver.

tools.name: bluetoothLENode
tools.description: Creates a Bluetooth LE network node (central, peripheral, broadcaster, observer or isochronous roles) with a full LE stack (LL, L2CAP-lite, PHY) for system-level simulation in wirelessNetworkSimulator; connections are configured with bluetoothLEConnectionConfig and traffic with networkTrafficOnOff, and statistics are collected with statistics(node).
tools.usage:
node = bluetoothLENode(role)
node = bluetoothLENode(role, Name=Value)
configureConnection(cfgConnection, centralNode, peripheralNode)
addTrafficSource(node, trafficSource, DestinationNode=peer)
stats = statistics(node)
tools.notes: Requires Bluetooth Toolbox and Communications Toolbox Wireless Network Simulation Library (R2022a+). bluetoothNode is the BR/EDR counterpart; coexistence with WLAN nodes (wlanNode) is supported.

tools.name: satelliteScenario
tools.description: Creates a satellite scenario that holds satellites, ground stations, platforms, sensors and links with a simulation start/stop time and sample time, propagating orbits (two-body Keplerian, SGP4/SDP4 from TLE, or numerical) and providing access, link and geometry analysis plus 3-D visualization via satelliteScenarioViewer.
tools.usage:
sc = satelliteScenario
sc = satelliteScenario(startTime, stopTime, sampleTime)
sc = satelliteScenario(___, AutoSimulate=false)

parameters.name: AutoSimulate
parameters.description: false to step manually with advance/restart.

parameters.name: Object functions
parameters.description: satellite, groundStation, platform, walkerStar, walkerDelta, access, aer, states, orbitalElements, play, satelliteScenarioViewer, advance, restart.

tools.notes: Requires Satellite Communications Toolbox (R2021a+). Times are UTC; use states(sat, t, CoordinateFrame='geographic') for lat/lon/alt.

tools.name: satellite
tools.description: Adds one or more satellites to a scenario from a TLE file, an RINEX/SEM/YUMA GNSS almanac, Keplerian orbital elements, or a timetable/timeseries of positions and velocities, selecting the orbit propagator (two-body-keplerian, sgp4, sdp4, ephemeris, numerical). Satellites are the source/target of access, link, aer and pointAt analyses.
tools.usage:
sat = satellite(sc, tleFile)
sat = satellite(sc, semiMajorAxis, eccentricity, inclination, RAAN, argOfPeriapsis, trueAnomaly)
sat = satellite(sc, positionTimetable)
sat = satellite(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: tleFile / almanac
parameters.description: TLE (.tle/.txt), RINEX (.rnx), SEM (.al3) or YUMA (.alm) file.

parameters.name: Orbital elements
parameters.description: Semi-major axis (m), eccentricity, inclination, RAAN, argument of periapsis, true anomaly (degrees).

tools.notes: Attach sensors and antennas with conicalSensor, transmitter, receiver, gaussianAntenna; orient with pointAt.

tools.name: groundStation
tools.description: Adds ground stations (fixed sites given by latitude, longitude and altitude with a minimum elevation angle) to a satellite scenario. Ground stations host receivers/transmitters and are used with access, link, aer and satelliteScenarioViewer to analyse visibility and link budgets from the ground segment.
tools.usage:
gs = groundStation(sc)
gs = groundStation(sc, lat, lon)
gs = groundStation(sc, Name=Value)

parameters.name: MinElevationAngle
parameters.description: Degrees; access requires elevation above this (default 0).

tools.notes: Introduced in R2021a. Use platform for moving ground/air/sea assets defined by trajectories.

tools.name: walkerStar
tools.description: Adds a Walker Star constellation (polar/near-polar planes spread over 180 degrees of RAAN, as in Iridium) to a satellite scenario from total satellites, number of planes and phasing; walkerDelta creates the 360-degree-spread variant (Galileo/Starlink style). Returns the satellite array for further configuration and analysis.
tools.usage:
sats = walkerStar(sc, radius, totalSatellites, geometryPlanes, phasing)
sats = walkerStar(___, inclination)
sats = walkerStar(___, Name=Value)
sats = walkerDelta(sc, radius, totalSatellites, geometryPlanes, phasing, inclination)

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Orbit radius in metres (Earth radius + altitude).

tools.notes: Introduced in R2023a. Large constellations slow the viewer; disable ShowDetails or use hide(sats).

tools.name: access
tools.description: Adds line-of-sight access analysis between two or more scenario assets (satellites, ground stations, platforms, sensors), returning an Access object whose accessStatus, accessIntervals and accessPercentage functions report when the geometric constraints (elevation mask, sensor field of view, Earth occlusion) are satisfied. Access lines are drawn in the viewer.
tools.usage:
ac = access(asset1, asset2)
ac = access(asset1, asset2, ..., assetN)   % multi-hop access
s = accessStatus(ac)
intvls = accessIntervals(ac)
p = accessPercentage(ac)

parameters.name: asset
parameters.description: satellite, groundStation, platform or conicalSensor objects (arrays allowed).

parameters.name: LineColor / LineWidth
parameters.description: Viewer display properties of the Access object.

tools.notes: Radio-link feasibility (Eb/No margin) is analysed with link/linkStatus/linkIntervals instead of pure geometric access.

tools.name: link
tools.description: Adds a communication link analysis between a transmitter and one or more receivers (optionally through repeaters/relays) in a satellite scenario; the Link object computes Eb/No over time (ebno), whether the required Eb/No is met (linkStatus, linkIntervals) and link percentage, taking antenna gains, pointing, free-space loss and optional propagation losses into account.
tools.usage:
lnk = link(tx, rx)
lnk = link(tx, rx1, rx2, ...)   % multi-hop
e = ebno(lnk)
s = linkStatus(lnk)
intvls = linkIntervals(lnk)

parameters.name: tx
parameters.description: transmitter object (Frequency, Power, BitRate, SystemLoss, antenna).

tools.notes: Add atmospheric attenuation from p618PropagationLosses to the link margin manually or via the satelliteCNR functions. pointAt(tx.Parent, gs) steers the antenna.

tools.name: aer
tools.description: Returns azimuth, elevation and range of a target asset as seen from an observer asset over the scenario time (or at specified times), in the observer's local frame; used for antenna pointing, visibility plots and doppler/delay computations between satellites, ground stations and platforms.
tools.usage:
[az, el, r] = aer(observer, target)
[az, el, r, timeOut] = aer(observer, target, timeIn)
[___] = aer(___, CoordinateFrame='ned' | 'body')

parameters.name: observer / target
parameters.description: satellite, groundStation, platform, gimbal or sensor objects.

parameters.name: timeIn
parameters.description: datetime scalar or vector within the scenario window.

tools.notes: states returns ECEF/inertial/geographic position and velocity; orbitalElements returns Keplerian elements at a time.

tools.name: satelliteScenarioViewer
tools.description: Opens a 3-D globe viewer for a satellite scenario showing satellites, orbits, ground tracks, ground stations, sensor footprints, access/link lines and a time control with playback speed; play(sc) animates the scenario in the viewer. Camera and display properties can be set programmatically and snapshots exported.
tools.usage:
v = satelliteScenarioViewer(sc)
v = satelliteScenarioViewer(sc, Name=Value)
play(sc)
campos(v, lat, lon, height)
show(sat, v); hide(sat, v)
tools.notes: The viewer requires Java/OpenGL; in headless batch mode skip visualization and rely on accessIntervals/ebno numerics.

tools.name: p618PropagationLosses
tools.description: Computes Earth-space propagation losses per ITU-R P.618 (rain attenuation, gaseous absorption, cloud/fog, scintillation and total attenuation with cross-polarization discrimination) for a site, frequency, elevation and availability, using the ITU digital maps that must be downloaded once with the P.618 support data. Essential for Ka/Ku-band link budgets.
tools.usage:
[pl, xpd] = p618PropagationLosses(cfg)
[pl, xpd] = p618PropagationLosses(cfg, Name=Value)

parameters.name: cfg
parameters.description: p618Config with Frequency, ElevationAngle, Latitude, Longitude, TotalAnnualExceedance (0.001..5 %), PolarizationTiltAngle, AntennaDiameter, AntennaEfficiency.

parameters.name: pl
parameters.description: Struct with Ag, Ac, Ar, As, At (dB).

tools.notes: Run p618SiteDiversityOutage for diversity gain. The maps are installed via the 'Download Digital Maps' link in the doc (MAT files placed on the path).

tools.name: gnssCACode
tools.description: Generates the 1023-chip coarse/acquisition (C/A) Gold code for one or more PRN indices of GPS, QZSS or NavIC satellites, returned as columns of +1/0 chips; used to build GPS L1 waveforms, correlators and acquisition/tracking simulations. gpsPCode generates the precision P-code.
tools.usage: code = gnssCACode(prnid, gnsstype)

parameters.name: prnid
parameters.description: PRN index or vector (GPS 1..210, QZSS 183..202, NavIC 1..14).

tools.example:
ca = gnssCACode([1 7 12], "GPS");     % 1023-by-3
chips = 1 - 2*ca;                     % map to +/-1
r = xcorr(chips(:,1), chips(:,2));    % low cross-correlation
tools.notes: Introduced in R2021b. Related: gpsWaveformGenerator (complete L1 C/A waveform), gnssSignalAcquirer and gnssSignalTracker for receivers.

tools.name: dvbs2WaveformGenerator
tools.description: System object that generates DVB-S2 baseband frames from input user packets or bits: BBFRAME processing (mode adaptation, BBHEADER, CRC), BCH and LDPC coding, bit interleaving, APSK/PSK modulation per MODCOD, physical-layer framing with pilots and scrambling, and root-raised-cosine pulse shaping. dvbs2xWaveformGenerator covers the DVB-S2X extensions.
tools.usage:
s2 = dvbs2WaveformGenerator
s2 = dvbs2WaveformGenerator(Name=Value)
waveform = s2(data)
info(s2)
tools.notes: Receiver-side helpers (dvbs2BitRecover, symbol timing/carrier recovery) are shown in the 'End-to-End DVB-S2 Simulation' example. Requires Satellite Communications Toolbox.
